Twelve of the fourteen edge ends stay within a team, 0.43 in each diagonal cell (accent); the single cross edge C–D puts 0.07 in each off-diagonal cell." width="100%"} The counts of `attribute_mixing_dict()` as a matrix: entry `[i][j]` is the fraction (or count) of edge ends joining a node with the `i`-th value to a node with the `j`-th value. A heavy diagonal means homophily; the nominal assortativity coefficient (`assortativity_nominal()`) is computed from exactly this matrix. NetworkX's `attribute_mixing_matrix()` returns only the matrix, ordered arbitrarily unless a `mapping=` is given. EdgeCase returns the matrix together with the attribute values labelling its rows and columns, sorted. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attribute]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the node attribute. Every node must have a value. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), entries sum to `1`. If `False`, they are counts. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[float]], list]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(matrix, values)`: the square matrix as a list of rows, and the attribute values labelling rows and columns, sorted (by their text if values are not comparable). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If some node has no value for the attribute. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~attribute_mixing_dict`) : The same counts as a nested dict. [](`~assortativity_nominal`) : The coefficient computed from this matrix. [](`~degree_mixing_matrix`) : The matrix for degree instead. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The counts of `attribute_mixing_dict()`, with a row and a column for each value, sorted: ::: {#685f79b0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) graph = graph.set_node_attrs( "team", {"A": "red", "B": "red", "C": "blue", "D": "blue"} ) matrix, teams = graph.attribute_mixing_matrix("team", normalized=False) teams, matrix ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['blue', 'red'], [[2.0, 1.0], [1.0, 2.0]]) ``` ::: ::: ### Bought together In `polbooks()`, two books about US politics are linked when Amazon customers often bought both, and the `leaning` attribute records each book's slant. As fractions of the links, counted from both ends, almost all the weight is on the diagonal for the conservative and liberal books, which are rarely bought together. The 13 neutral books are the exception, with most of their links to one side or the other: ::: {#2a55e4fb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl books = ec.polbooks() matrix, leanings = books.attribute_mixing_matrix("leaning") pl.DataFrame( [[round(v, 2) for v in row] for row in matrix], schema=leanings, orient="row", ).insert_column(0, pl.Series("leaning", leanings)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
